result:
The admin push tools now read and delete subscriptions through `pushStore(env)` (D1), and the test reports its result per subscription. I committed this in Orbit-Core only, and `npm test` is green (1480 pass, 10 skipped). I haven't sent a real push, so whether the test now reaches Jay's iPhone is unconfirmed.

- **Storage:** `push-test`, `pushes`, `broadcast`, account delete, `pushRecords` and the cleanup in `eco-admin.js` no longer touch `env.RATE_LIMIT_KV` for subscriptions. `pushStore.list` only returned keys with a notice due, so listing every subscription needed a new `{ prefix, all: true }` option in `push.js`.
- **Per-subscription result:** `push-test` now answers with one plain-language line for each case:
  - no subscription for this pass and app;
  - accepted by Apple or the push service;
  - gone (404/410), in which case the subscription is also removed;
  - failed, with its status code.
- **Admin page:** `site/admin/index.html` shows that line where the test starts. Failures show in red.
- **Scope and slug:** I changed nothing here, because I found no mismatch.
  - The `/app/` service worker is registered from `/app/`, so its scope is `/app/`.
  - `enablePush` in `kit/orbit.mjs` already uses that worker's registration when running inside Orbit.
  - Each framed app saves the subscription under its own slug (`s.app`), and the admin test looks under the app you pick, so the two agree.
- **Tests:** the new `tests/admin-push.test.mjs` covers the no-subscription, gone-and-removed, result-mapping and list/broadcast cases. It uses a KV that fails on any read, write or delete, so a KV regression would show. It also checks the `/app/` scope and slug wiring by reading the source text.
- **MAP.md:** it already said pushes live in D1. I added how the admin tools reach them and how `/app/` subscribes. I also renamed the cleanup label from "通知訂閱（KV）" to "通知訂閱".

- **Left:**
  - The account-delete assertion in the new test is loose. It only checks the push count if `deleteAccount` succeeds against the fake store.
  - If the test says Apple accepted it but nothing appears, the cause is outside the Worker. Check the iPhone's notification settings and that the home-screen app has notifications on.
